newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Chiluba sets poll date, Zambians riot.
newsitem.headline: Chiluba sets poll date, Zambians riot.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba set November 18 as the date for elections on Saturday but sparked a riot among his supporters when he named an unpopular candidate for one constituency.
Police fired tear gas and lashed out with batons as people at a rally addressed by Chiluba in the central mining town of Kabwe rampaged through the town centre, barricading roads and starting fires.
Witnesses said hundreds of supporters of the ruling Movement for Multi-party Elections (MMD) took part in the riot in protest at Chiluba's choice of a parliamentary candidate for Kabwe.
Chiluba abandoned the rally, leaving in a motorcade with a strong security escort, after hecklers jeered his candidate selection.
He started his address by setting the date for elections which were due to have been held by the end of October.
"I am happy to announce that the presidential and parliamentary elections shall be held be held on November 18," he said.
He said parliament had been dissolved on October 18 ahead of the elections.
Chiluba said constitutional amendments earlier this year allowed his government to stay in office for up to three months beyond the expiry of its five-year term on October 31.

"I remain president before during and after the elections. And before I hand over power to myself or somebody else, I will still be in power. There will be no vacuum. I will still be in power," he said.
Opposition parties and the Law Association of Zambia have said there would be a power vacuum in the country if elections were not held by the end of October.
Dean Mungomba, leader of the opposition Zambia Democratic Congress, speaking before Chiluba's remarks on Saturday, said:
"On October 31, Mr Chiluba's term of office comes to an end. No amount of legal gymnastics can change that fact.
"We shall have no recognition of this government after October 31, and therefore reserve the right to take whatever steps to ensure he does not extend his stay in office beyond October 31."
Chiluba's government has already angered its opponents by amending the constitution to prevent anyone who has served two terms as president from running again.
This rules out Kenneth Kaunda, head of the opposition United National Independence Party (UNIP) who led Zambia to independence from Britain in 1964.
